the population ecology of two hole-nesters, the great tit (Parus major) and the pied flycatchers (Ficedula hypoleuca), in Europe.
the influence of climate on population dynamics of two European hole nesting passerine species.
the effects of climate variation on the dynamics of populations of two hole-nester passerines.

the population dynamics of both species were more sensitive to climate at higher latitudes, but the relative contribution of the NAO to the population fluctuations of the two species varied with latitude.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the population dynamics of hole-nesting passerings are strongly affected by climate variation and that this effect increases towards the north in the great tit, whereas it remains constant in the pied flycatchers.
the population dynamics of hole-nesting species is strongly influenced by the North Atlantic Oscillations, but that this influence varies with latitude.
the effects of climate change on population dynamics of species will depend on the species' life history traits, the environmental stochasticity and on the climate pattern that is changing.

latitudinal gradients are likely to arise in the population dynamics as a result of the regional variation in the contribution of the stochastic factors to the population fluctuations.
